audit.title: Getting Started (Solana)

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens well — "Chainlink CCIP supports Solana through the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM), enabling cross-chain interoperability" is a clean liftable sentence. Weak point: the "Getting Started" section is a single-sentence redirect with no self-contained answer.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean H2 hierarchy, 0 level skips, sensible bullets. Sections are coherent but so short (median 39 words) that several chunks carry little standalone value.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Poor — 3 numerals, 0 with units, no version strings, no chain selectors, no mainnet/devnet names, no program IDs. This is the highest-lift gap.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 3 links, 1 opaque ("here"), 0 primary sources. No link to Solana docs, SVM spec, or the CCIP architecture/config pages.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: The SVM support sentence and the CCT bullet are liftable; adequate for a page this size.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: No JSON-LD, no canonical URL, no `inLanguage`, no og/twitter tags. A visible "Last Updated: 2025-08-22" exists in body but not as structured `dateModified`.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code blocks. For a "Getting Started" page, at least a minimal install/config or chain-selector snippet is expected; agents get nothing runnable here.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "what can I build" and "how do I start" at a surface level; no troubleshooting, no "which networks are supported," no prerequisites. Lifecycle is truncated at "use."

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. Consistent naming of CCIP/SVM/CCT.

audit.summary: This is a thin (172-word) landing/hub page that introduces CCIP support for Solana and routes readers to tutorials. Its biggest strength is a clean, quotable opening definition and clear structure; its biggest weakness is near-total absence of concrete specifics (no supported networks, addresses, chain selectors, or versions) and no code, which starves generative engines of liftable, attributable facts. As a getting-started page it under-delivers on the setup→use→debug lifecycle and will lose retrieval to richer sibling/tutorial pages. Honest verdict: functional as a signpost, weak as a standalone GEO asset.

recommendations.title: Add concrete supported-network specifics
recommendations.issue: "enabling cross-chain interoperability between Solana and other blockchain families" — no specifics
recommendations.change: Add a table/list naming supported Solana networks (e.g., Solana mainnet-beta, Devnet), their CCIP chain selectors, router program IDs, and the earliest supported release/version. State any current limitations (e.g., token-only vs. arbitrary messaging status) with numbers.
recommendations.why: Quantitative, entity-specific facts are the highest-lift change for citation; this page currently offers none.

recommendations.title: Add symptom-/intent-phrased headings and an FAQ
recommendations.where: New H2s after "What You Can Build"
recommendations.issue: No coverage of "Which Solana networks does CCIP support?", "How do I send a message from Solana to an EVM chain?", prerequisites, or common setup errors
recommendations.change: Add short Q-phrased H2/H3 sections mirroring how devs query, each answered in the first sentence, then linking to the relevant tutorial.
recommendations.why: Question-phrased headings win symptom/intent retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Fix opaque links and add primary-source citations
recommendations.where: "Getting Started with Solana CCIP" and the SVM support paragraph
recommendations.issue: "SVM tutorials can be found [here]" — opaque anchor; 0 primary sources
recommendations.change: Replace "here" with descriptive text ("see the **Solana (SVM) CCIP tutorials**"); add inline links to the CCIP architecture page, the CCT standard page, and the canonical Solana/SVM documentation.
recommendations.why: Descriptive, authoritative links raise credibility and citation rate; opaque anchors carry no retrieval signal.

recommendations.title: Add TechArticle JSON-LD, canonical URL, and structured dateModified
recommendations.issue: JSON-LD 0 blocks; canonical MISSING; dateModified absent (only body "Last Updated")
recommendations.change: Emit `TechArticle` JSON-LD with `headline`, `dateModified: 2025-08-22`, `inLanguage: en`, and a self-referential canonical URL.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness signals improve agent parsing and E-E-A-T trust.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal runnable starting snippet
recommendations.issue: 0 code blocks on a getting-started page
recommendations.change: Add one language-tagged snippet showing a minimal CCIP-on-Solana action (e.g., resolving a chain selector or the router program ID with a config), with imports/versions.
recommendations.why: Getting-started queries expect copy-pasteable starters; agents cannot act on prose-only redirects.

antiPatterns: Opaque link text: "SVM tutorials can be found **here**."
Thin redirect section: "Getting Started with Solana CCIP" is a one-line pointer with no standalone content.
Freshness date present in body text but not machine-readable (`dateModified` absent).
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced from the page — good; ensure this URL is listed in it and in the sitemap.
JSON-LD/canonical are site-template concerns; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` so schema can be verified rather than inferred absent.
As a hub page, its retrieval value depends on internal links from the richer SVM tutorial pages pointing back here (canonical-hub pattern) — an off-page linking task.
